hero.headline: Scripture that takes you seriously.
hero.subhead: A literary Bible translation for those who refuse to choose between intellectual honesty and living faith.

manifesto.p1: Somewhere along the way, we were told to choose: study the Bible critically and risk losing the sacred, or hold onto faith and stop asking hard questions.
manifesto.p2: We don't believe that's the only way.
manifesto.p3: Aperto is a literary translation—poetry as poetry, prose as prose—with ancient context woven directly into the text, clearly marked so you always know what was written and what it meant.
manifesto.p4: It's built on ecumenical scholarship from Catholic, Protestant, Orthodox, and Pentecostal traditions.
manifesto.p5: And it's designed for real encounter—through audio, music, and meditation shaped by how people actually read and grow today.
manifesto.p9: For the curious and the seeking. For those who left and those who stayed. For anyone ready to look again.

getInvolved.title: Get Involved
getInvolved.description: Aperto is an open project—and it grows through people who want to be part of it. Whether that's translation, audio production, feedback, or something else entirely: every form of involvement is welcome.

falseChoice.title: The False Choice
falseChoice.p1: For a long time, Christianity has felt like it's splitting into two camps.
falseChoice.p2: One takes the text seriously—historically, critically, honestly. It asks hard questions about authorship, context, transmission. It refuses easy answers. But somewhere along the way, it often loses the expectation that Scripture might actually do something to you. Study becomes analysis. The text becomes an artifact.
falseChoice.p3: The other promises encounter, transformation, a living word. It expects God to show up. But it sometimes asks you to stop asking questions—or at least to feel guilty about them. Certainty becomes the measure of faith. Curiosity feels like betrayal.
falseChoice.p4: We think that's a false choice.
falseChoice.p5: The scholars who first studied these texts were monks in prayer. The mystics who encountered God in them were rigorous readers. For most of Christian history, depth of study and depth of encounter weren't opposites—they were the same path.

literary.title: A literary translation
literary.desc: that honors the original forms—poetry as poetry, narrative as narrative, letter as letter. Scripture is literature before it's anything else, and we translate it that way.

context.title: Context made visible
context.desc: The first readers of these texts understood things we don't—cultural assumptions, geographic references, religious background, literary echoes. We weave that context directly into the text, clearly formatted so you always know what was written and what it meant. No more flipping to footnotes to understand why something matters.

ecumenical.title: Ecumenical foundations
ecumenical.desc: Our exegesis draws on Catholic, Protestant, Orthodox, and Pentecostal scholarship. Not to flatten differences, but because the text belongs to the whole Church, and every tradition sees something the others might miss.

multimedia.title: Multimedia encounter
multimedia.desc: Audio Bible. Podcasts that unpack each passage. Original songs that capture the emotional weight of the text. Meditations and devotions. Scripture isn't just read—it's heard, sung, sat with, lived.

design.title: Designed for how people actually engage
design.desc: Informed by research on digital reading and spiritual formation, we build formats that work with attention, not against it—and that support genuine growth, not just information transfer.

europe.title: Scripture for Europe
europe.desc: Available in 11 languages and growing—bringing resources to communities that have waited too long for translations that are both serious and alive.

ai.title: Made possible by AI
ai.desc: Thoughtful workflows let us achieve depth and scale that would otherwise take generations. What once seemed impossible for smaller language communities is now within reach.

audience.title: Who This Is For
audience.skeptic: For the skeptic who still wonders.
audience.believer: For the believer who still thinks.
audience.left: For those who left the church but couldn't leave the questions.
audience.stayed: For those who stayed but feel the tension.
audience.curious: For the spiritually curious and the intellectually honest.
audience.closing: You don't have to have it figured out. You just have to be willing to look.

europe.title: A European Project
europe.p1: Christianity in Europe sits at a crossroads. Historic churches face decline. Evangelical communities remain small. Secular culture has often written off faith as intellectually untenable—and too many expressions of Christianity have confirmed that suspicion.
europe.p2: But there's also hunger. People searching for meaning, for depth, for something that can hold the weight of real life. People who might be open to the Christian story if someone offered it without asking them to stop thinking.
europe.p3: Aperto is built for that moment. A Bible that urban, educated, questioning Europeans can engage without embarrassment—and that might just change them.
europe.p4: We're starting with 11 languages. We won't stop there.

join.title: Join Us
join.p1: We're building this one chapter at a time, one book at a time. Right now, you can read Luke 1—the announcement of John the Baptist, Gabriel's visit to Mary, and two songs that changed the world.
join.p2: Come see what we're making. Bring your doubts. Bring your longing.
join.goDeeperDesc: Learn how we translate, how our AI workflows function, and the scholarship behind every decision.

challenge.title: The Challenge
challenge.p1: Translating Scripture well has always required holding tensions together: fidelity to the original and accessibility to the reader, scholarly rigor and spiritual vitality, respect for tradition and openness to fresh insight.
challenge.p2: Aperto adds one more: the scale to serve Europe's diverse language communities, and the depth that usually requires decades of work per language.
challenge.p3: We believe we've found a way to hold all of these together.

literary.title: Literature First
literary.desc: The Bible is poetry, narrative, letter, prophecy, law, wisdom literature, apocalyptic vision. Each genre has its own rhythm, its own logic, its own way of meaning. We translate poetry as poetry—with line breaks, metaphor, and sound. We translate prose as prose—with narrative momentum and natural speech. The form carries meaning; we honor both.

context.title: Context Made Visible
context.desc: The original readers of these texts understood things modern readers don't: cultural customs, geographic references, religious background, literary echoes from earlier Scripture. Most translations force you into footnotes to recover this. We weave essential context directly into the text—using clear formatting so you always know what was written and what it meant. You see the text as ancient readers experienced it, without losing sight of what the text actually says.

ecumenical.title: Ecumenical Foundation
ecumenical.desc: Our exegetical foundation draws on Catholic, Protestant, Orthodox, and Pentecostal scholarship. Not to erase differences—they matter—but because every tradition illuminates something others might miss. The text belongs to the whole Church. Our process reflects that.

engagement.title: Designed for Real Engagement
engagement.desc: We don't just think about what to say—we think about how people actually read and grow. Informed by research on digital attention and spiritual formation, we design formats that work with how people engage today: scannable when needed, immersive when invited, multi-sensory across audio, music, and meditation.

pentecost.title: The Pentecost Impulse
pentecost.p1: The Spirit's first public act was crossing a language barrier. At Pentecost, people from every nation "heard in their own language" (Acts 2:8). The miracle wasn't just power—it was accessibility. From the beginning, God has shown that his word is meant for everyone, in forms they can understand.
pentecost.p2: That's the heartbeat of translation. And it's the conviction driving Aperto: every European language community deserves Scripture resources with real depth—not just bare text, but the context, scholarship, and multimedia that bring it alive.

reformation.title: The Reformation Precedent
reformation.p1: The Reformers believed the plowboy had as much right to Scripture as the priest. That conviction required new technology—the printing press—and was fiercely resisted by religious authorities who feared what would happen when ordinary people could read for themselves.
reformation.p2: They were right to sense that everything would change. They were wrong to resist it.
reformation.p3: Every expansion of Scripture access has followed this pattern: vernacular translation, printing, audio, digital. Each was initially suspect. Each was eventually embraced. Each extended the reach of God's word to people who had been excluded—by language, by literacy, by cost, by geography.
reformation.p4: AI-assisted translation stands in this lineage. The technology is new. The conviction is ancient.

unexpected.title: God's Pattern of Unexpected Means
unexpected.p1: Scripture is full of God working through unlikely instruments:
unexpected.donkey: A donkey speaks to a prophet (Numbers 22)
unexpected.pagan: A pagan king is called God's "anointed" (Isaiah 45:1)
unexpected.astrologers: Foreign astrologers are led to the Messiah (Matthew 2)
unexpected.foolish: "The foolish things of the world shame the wise" (1 Corinthians 1:27)
unexpected.p2: When Jesus said "if these were silent, the very stones would cry out" (Luke 19:40), he was making a point about inevitability: God's truth will find its way out. If expected voices fall short, unexpected ones will rise.
unexpected.p3: We don't claim AI is the stones crying out. But we do believe that when the need is real and traditional means can't meet it, God opens new paths. He's done it before. We believe he's doing it again.
unexpected.blockquote: Silicon chips are, after all, rocks we taught to think. Sand refined, etched with circuits, trained on humanity's collected wisdom. If God can speak through a burning bush, a donkey, or bread and wine—perhaps silicon isn't so strange a medium.

silence.title: The European Silence
silence.p1: Europe was once the heart of Christian civilization. Today it's one of the most secular continents on earth—and one of the most underserved when it comes to quality Scripture resources.
silence.p2: The silence here isn't primarily rejection. It's incapacity.
silence.p3: Historic churches often have institutional resources but declining energy—and sometimes theological ambivalence about whether Scripture still transforms. Evangelical and charismatic communities have conviction but lack scale and infrastructure. Smaller language communities—Danish, Swedish, Polish, Portuguese, Ukrainian—simply cannot sustain the decades of scholarly work required for resources of this depth.
silence.p4: The need is vast. Traditional capacity is insufficient. Not because people are unfaithful, but because the economics don't work and the demographics have shifted.

possible.title: What AI Makes Possible
possible.p1: A translation of this depth—literary, contextually enriched, multimedia-rich, ecumenically grounded—would normally require a generation of work per language. For most European communities, it would never happen at all.
possible.p2: AI doesn't replace human judgment. It multiplies it. Every exegetical decision, every translation choice, every footnote still passes through human review. But the scale becomes possible. Eleven languages now. More to come. Resources that smaller communities could never produce on their own—finally within reach.
possible.p3: What seemed impossible is now feasible. Communities that have waited generations might not have to wait any longer.
possible.p4: We believe that matters. We believe God cares about it. And we believe he's given us tools to do something about it.

step1.title: Deep Exegesis
step1.desc: Comprehensive scholarly research for each passage: Greek text analysis, major commentaries across traditions, lexicons, cultural and historical studies, patristic sources. This is the foundation everything else builds on.

step2.title: Literary Translation Draft
step2.desc: AI-assisted drafting filtered through our translation philosophy—literary, accessible, faithful. The goal: language worthy of being read aloud, not just decoded.

step3.title: Contextual Enrichment
step3.desc: Identification and integration of cultural, geographic, religious, and literary context the original audience would have known. Clearly formatted to distinguish from the biblical text itself.

step4.title: Footnotes & Exegesis
step4.desc: Deeper layers for those who want them: Greek word choices, scholarly debates, historical background, and honest acknowledgment of uncertainty and interpretive options.

step5.title: Multimedia Production
step5.desc: Audio Bible narration. Podcasts unpacking each pericope. Original songs capturing the emotional and theological weight of key passages. Meditations and devotional guides. Scripture experienced, not just read.

step6.title: Human Review & Refinement
step6.desc: Every output passes through human review. AI generates drafts; humans correct, refine, and approve. The judgment is always human.

step7.title: Community Feedback
step7.desc: Ongoing revision based on reader response and scholarly input. Translation is never finished—it's a living conversation.

honesty.title: Honesty
honesty.desc: We don't hide complexity, smooth over difficulties, or pretend certainty where there is none. The text is stranger and more challenging than many translations let on. We let it be.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.desc: Every sentence should be understandable without insider vocabulary or assumed religious background. Clarity isn't dumbing down—it's hospitality.

craft.title: Literary Craft
craft.desc: Language worthy of the text. Not just information transferred, but writing that rewards reading—rhythm, imagery, weight.

expectancy.title: Spiritual Expectancy
expectancy.desc: We study rigorously because we believe the text can still transform. Scholarship serves encounter, not the other way around.

humility.title: Ecumenical Humility
humility.desc: We learn from traditions beyond our own. We acknowledge what we don't know. We hold our interpretations with open hands.
